1.1: There was a man in the land of Ausitis whose name was Job. That man was true, blameless, righteous, and God-fearing, and he abstained from every evil thing.
1.2: Now he had seven sons and three daughters,
1.3: and his cattle consisted of seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys in the pastures. Moreover he possessed a very large number of house servants. His works were also great on the earth, and that man was the most noble of all the men of the East.
1.4: His sons would visit one another and prepare a banquet every day, and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
1.5: When the days of their drinking were ended, Job sent and purified them; and he rose early in the morning and offered sacrifices for them according to their number, as well as one calf for the sins of their souls. For Job said, “Lest my sons consider evil things in their mind against God.” Therefore Job did this continually. Satan Is Permitted to Test Job
1.6: Then as it so happened one day that behold, the angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the devil also came with them.
1.7: The Lord said to the devil, “Where did you come from?” So the devil answered the Lord and said, “I came here after going about the earth and walking around under heaven.”
1.8: Then the Lord said to him, “Have you yet considered my servant Job, since there is none like him on the earth: a blameless, true, and God-fearing man, and one who abstains from every evil thing?”
1.9: So the devil answered and said before the Lord, “Does Job worship the Lord for no reason?
1.10: Have You not made a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his cattle have increased in the land.
1.11: But stretch out Your hand and touch all he has, and see if he will bless You to Your face.”
1.12: Then the Lord said to the devil, “Behold, whatever he has I give into your hand; but do not touch him.” Thus the devil went out from the Lord. Job Loses His Children and Property
1.13: Now there was a day when Job's sons and daughters were drinking wine in the house of their elder brother,
1.14: and behold, a messenger came to Job and said, “The yokes of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were feeding beside them.
1.15: Then raiders came and took them captive and killed the servants with the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
1.16: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep, and likewise consumed the shepherds; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
1.17: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Horsemen formed three bands against us, surrounded the camels, took them captive, and killed the servants with the sword. I alone have escaped to tell you!”
1.18: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine with their elder brother,
1.19: and suddenly a great wind came from the desert and struck the four corners of the house; and it fell on your children, and they died; and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
1.20: Then Job arose, tore his robe, and shaved off the hair of his head; and he fell to the ground and worshiped, saying,
1.21: “Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return. The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away. As it seemed good to the Lord, so also it came to pass. Blessed be the name of the Lord.”
1.22: In all these things that happened, Job did not sin against the Lord or charge God with folly. Job Loses His Health

2.1: Then again as it so happened another day, the angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the devil also came among them to present himself before the Lord.
2.2: The Lord said to the devil, “Where did you come from?” Then the devil said before the Lord, “I came here from walking around under heaven and going about all the earth.”
2.3: Then the Lord said to the devil, “Have you considered my servant Job, since there is none like him on the earth: an innocent, true, blameless, and God-fearing man, and one who abstains from every evil thing? Moreover he still holds fast to his integrity, though you told me to destroy his possessions without cause.”
2.4: Then the devil answered the Lord and said, “Skin for skin. Whatever a man has he will pay in full for his life.
2.5: Yet truly, stretch out Your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and see if he will bless You to Your face.”
2.6: So the Lord said to the devil, “Behold, I give him over to you; only spare his life.”
2.7: Thus the devil went out from the Lord and struck Job with malignant sores from head to foot.
2.8: So he took a potsherd to scrape away the discharge and sat on a dunghill outside the city.
2.9: When a period of time passed, his wife said to him, “How long will you hold out, saying,
2.10: ‘Behold, I will wait a little longer, looking for the hope of my salvation’?
2.11: Listen, your memory is wiped out from the earth: your sons and daughters, the pangs and pains of my womb, which I suffered in vain and with hardships.
2.12: You yourself are sitting down, spending the nights in the open air among the rottenness of worms;
2.13: and I go about as a wanderer and a handmaid from place to place and from house to house, waiting for the setting of the sun, so as to rest from my labors and pains that now beset me.
2.14: But say a word against the Lord and die!”
2.15: Then Job looked at her and said, “You have spoken as one of the foolish women speaks. If we accepted good things from the Lord's hand, shall we not endure evil things?” In all these things that happened to him, Job did not sin with his lips against God. Job's Friends Visit Him
2.16: Now when Job's three friends heard of all the evil things that had come upon him, each one came to him from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite king, Bildad the Shuhite ruler, and Zophar the Naamathite king. For they came to him with one accord: to visit and comfort him.
2.17: Now when they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him; and they cried with a loud voice and wept. Each one tore his robe and sprinkled dust on his head.
2.18: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke to him, for they saw that his affliction was terrible and very great. Job Curses His Day of Birth

3.3: After this, Job opened his mouth 2and cursed his day, saying: 3 “May the day perish on which I was born, And the night in which they said, ‘Behold, a male child.’
3.4: May that day be darkness, And may the Lord not regard it from above; Nor may the light come upon it.
3.5: May darkness and the shadow of death seize it; May a cloud settle on it.
3.6: May that day and night be cursed; May darkness carry it away; May it not come into the days of the year; May it not be numbered with the days of the month.
3.7: But may that night be sorrow, And may no gladness come upon it, nor joy.
3.8: But may he who curses that day curse it, Even he who is about to subdue the great sea-m onster.
3.9: May the stars of that night be darkened, And may it remain dark. May it not come into the light, And may it not see the morning star arise;
3.10: Because it did not shut up the doors of mym other's womb, For it would have removed sorrow from my eyes.
3.11: Why did I not die in the womb? Why did I not perish immediately when I came from the womb?
3.12: Why did the knees receive me, And why did I nurse the breasts?
3.13: For now I would have been lying down and quiet; I would have slept and been at rest
3.14: With kings and counselors of the earth Who were insolent with their swords,
3.15: Or with rulers who had abundant gold And filled their houses with silver;
3.16: Or I would have been like an untimely birth Proceeding from his m other's womb, Or like infants who never saw the light.
3.17: There the ungodly have burnt out the fury of wrath; There the weary in body are at rest.
3.18: There men of ancient times have ceased together To hear the voice of those who collect taxes.
3.19: The small and great are there, And the servant who feared his master.
3.20: Why is light given to those in bitterness, And life to souls in pain,
3.21: Who long for death, but do not obtain it, Digging for it like treasures,
3.22: And would be very joyful if they could obtain it?
3.23: Death is a rest to such a man, For God is against him.
3.24: For groaning comes before my food; And I weep and am oppressed with terror.
3.25: For the terror I was concerned about came to me, And what I feared happened to me;
3.26: Neither was I at peace or quiet, nor at rest, For wrath came upon me.” Eliphaz Accuses Job

4.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
4.2: “Hav e you been often spoken to in distress? But now who shall endure the force of your words?
4.3: For though you instructed many, And strengthened the hands of the weak one,
4.4: And raised up the sick with your words, And imparted courage to feeble knees,
4.5: Yet now pain has come upon you and touched you; And you are anxious.
4.6: Is not your fear, your hope, And the integrity of your way of life changed into folly?
4.7: Can you remember anyone pure who has perished, Or true people who were altogether uprooted?
4.8: According to what I have seen, those who plowharmful things and those who sow them Will reap pain for themselves.
4.9: They will perish by the command of the Lord, And they will be destroy ed by the breath of His wrath.
4.10: The strength of the lion, the voice of the lioness, And the exulting cry of dragons are extinguished.
4.11: The old lion has perished for lack of prey, And the cubs of the lioness have left one another.
4.12: “But if there had been any truth in your words, None of these evils would have befallen you. Shall not my ear receive extraordinary things from him?
4.13: But just as when terror falls upon men With dread at a noise in the night,
4.14: Shivering and trembling befell me And caused my bones to shake.
4.15: Then a spirit came before my face, And my hair and flesh shook with fear.
4.16: I arose, but could not recognize it. I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, But rather a gentle breeze, and a voice, saying,
4.17: ‘What? Shall a mortal man be pure in the Lord's sight, Or blameless before Him in his works?
4.18: If He puts no trust in His servants, And if He observes a perverse way in His angels,
4.19: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, Of whom we also are formed of the same clay? Does not He smite them like a moth?
4.20: They no longer exist from morning till evening; They have perished, for they cannot help themselves.
4.21: For He blows upon them, and they are withered. They have perished for lack of wisdom.’

5.1: Blessed Is He Whom God Has Reproved “But call out, if there is anyone who will obey you, Or if you shall see any of the holy angels.
5.2: For wrath destroy sa foolish man, And envy slays one who is deceived.
5.3: I have seen foolish people taking root, But suddenly their mode of life consumed them.
5.4: May their children be far from salvation, May they be derided at the gates of worse people, And may there be no one to deliver them.
5.5: For the righteous will eat what they have gathered, But they themselves will not be delivered from calamities. Their strength will be exhausted.
5.6: For trouble does not come from the earth, Nor does suffering spring from the mountains;
5.7: Yet man is born for trouble As the young bird is born to fly to high places.
5.8: But surely as for me, I will beseech the Lord, And call upon the Lord and Master of all,
5.9: Who does great, incomprehensible, And marvelous things without number.
5.10: He causes rain on the earth And sends water on all the places under the heaven.
5.11: He sets the lowly on high And raises up the lost.
5.12: He frustrates the counsels of the crafty So their hands cannot carry out their plans.
5.13: He catches the wise in their craftiness And subverts the counsel of the cunning.
5.14: Let them encounter darkness in the daytime, And may they grope at noontime as though it were night.
5.15: May they perish in war, But may the weak escape from the hand of the mighty.
5.16: May the weak have hope, And may the mouth of the unrighteous be stopped.
5.17: “But blessed is the man whom God corrects; Therefore, do not reject the chastening of the Almighty.
5.18: For He causes a man to be in pain, But He restores him again. He smites, but His hands heal.
5.19: Six times He shall deliver you out of troubles, And in seven no harm shall touch you.
5.20: In famine He shall deliver you from death, And in war He shall free you from the power of the sword.
5.21: He shall hide you from the scourge of the tongue, And you shall not be afraid of evils when they come.
5.22: You shall laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless, And you shall not be afraid of the wild animals of the earth.
5.23: For the wild animals of the field shall be at peace with you.
5.24: Then you shall know your house will be at peace with you; And in your dwelling place there shall be nothing amiss.
5.25: You shall also know your seed shall be many, And your children shall be like the grass of the earth.
5.26: You shall come to the grave as grain reaped in its season, Or as a heap of threshed wheat harvested at the proper time.
5.27: Behold, we have searched this out; This is what we have heard. Know for yourself if you have done anything wrong.” Mercy Has Rejected Me

6.2: “I wish there were someone who would weigh the wrath upon me, And at the same time lift up my griefs on a scale.
6.3: For indeed they would be heavier than the sand of the seashore; But as it seems, my words are worthless.
6.4: For the arrows of the Lord are in my body, Whose anger drinks my blood; For when I begin to speak, they pierce me.
6.5: What then? Will the wild donkey bray for no reason If he is not seeking food? Or will the ox moo at the manger when it has fodder?
6.6: Will bread be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in empty words?
6.7: My soul cannot stop groaning, For I see my food to be like the smell of a lion.
6.8: “Would that my request would come about, And the Lord would grant my hope.
6.9: Let the Lord begin and wound me, But let Him not utterly destroy me.
6.10: May the grave be my city upon the walls which I have leaped. I will not turn away from it, For I have not lied about the holy words of my God.
6.11: What strength do I have, that I should continue? For how long would my soul endure?
6.12: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh made of bronze?
6.13: Or have I not trusted in Him? But help is far from me.
6.14: “Mercy has rejected me; And the visitation of the Lord has disregarded me.
6.15: My relatives pay no attention to me. They pass me by like a wave, Or as though I were a failing brook.
6.16: Those who once reverenced me Now look upon me like snow or frozen ice.
6.17: For when it melts at the approach of the heat, It is no longer recognized for what it was.
6.18: Thus I have been forsaken by all, But I am also lost and homeless.
6.19: Look at the ways of Temanites, You who mark the paths of Sabeans.
6.20: Those who put their trust in cities and wealth Will be debtors to shame.
6.21: But you have also come to me without mercy, That seeing my wound you were afraid.
6.22: What? Have I ever made any demand of you? Or do I need your strength
6.23: To deliver me from enemies, Or to rescue me from the hand of the mighty?
6.24: “Teach me, and I will keep quiet. Tell me wherein I have erred.
6.25: But as it seems, the words of a true man are worthless, For I do not ask strength of you.
6.26: Neither will your rebuke cause me to cease my words, Nor will I endure the sound of your word.
6.27: Nevertheless you attack the orphan, And you jumpon your friend.
6.28: Now therefore, after I looked on your faces, I will not lie.
6.29: Sit down now, and may there be no wrongdoing; And come together again with a righteous man.
6.30: There is no wrongdoing on my tongue, Or does not my throat cultivate understanding?

7.1: My Life Is Vain “Is not the life of a man on earth an ordeal? Is not his life also like the life of a hired man working by the day,
7.2: Or like a servant who fears his master, Or like one who grasps for a shadow, Or like a hired man who eagerly looks for his wages?
7.3: So I have been enduring months of futility, And agonizing nights have been appointed for me.
7.4: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will it be day?’ When I arise, I say, ‘When will it be evening?’ I am full of pains from evening to morning.
7.5: My body is covered with loathsome worms, And I am wasting away As I scrape off clods of dust from my eruption.
7.6: “My life is lighter than speech And perishes with an empty hope.
7.7: Remember then, my life is a breath, And my eye will no longer return to see good.
7.8: The eye of him who sees me will not see me again; Your eyes are on me, I am no more.
7.9: I am like the cloud that cleared away from the sky, For if a man goes down to Hades, he shall not come up again.
7.10: He shall not return to his own house, Nor shall his place know him anymore.
7.11: “Now then, neither will I restrain my mouth. I will speak by necessity, Because I will disclose the bitterness of my soul When I am oppressed.
7.12: Am I a sea, or a serpent, That You set a guard over me?
7.13: I said, ‘My bed will comfort me, And on my couch I will counsel privately with myself.’
7.14: You scare me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
7.15: You will separate life from my spirit, Yet keep my bones from death.
7.16: For I will not live forever, that I should patiently endure. Let me alone, for my life is vain.
7.17: “What is man, that You should exalt him, Or that You should set Your heart on him,
7.18: Or that You should visit him every morning And judge him till the time of rest?
7.19: How long will You neither let me alone, Nor let me go until I swallow my saliva in grief?
7.20: If I have sinned, what can I do to You, O You who understand the heart of men? Why have You set me as Your accuser? Why am I a burden to You?
7.21: Why then have You not forgotten my lawlessness And purged my sin? But now I will depart into the earth, And in the morning I will no longer be here.” Bildad: The Ungodly Will Perish

8.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
8.2: “How long will you speak these things, And the breath of your mouth be filled with words?
8.3: Will the Lord do wrong when He judges, Or will He who made all things trouble righteousness?
8.4: If your sons sinned against Him, He sent them away because of their lawlessness.
8.5: But come early in the morning And make your supplication to the Lord Almighty.
8.6: If you are pure and true, He will hear your supplication And restore to you the dwelling of the righteous.
8.7: Though your beginning shall be small, Your latter end will be abundantly great.
8.8: For inquire about the form er generation And search am ong the race of our fathers;
8.9: For we are of yesterday and know nothing, Because our life on earth is a shadow.
8.10: Will they not teach you and proclaim to you, And bring forth words from their heart?
8.11: “Can the papyrus bloom without water, Or can the reeds flourish without moisture?
8.12: While it is still on the root and not yet harvested, Does not any vegetation wither before it receives moisture?
8.13: So shall be the end of all who forget the Lord, For the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
8.14: For his house shall be without inhabitants, And his tent shall turn out to be a spider's web.
8.15: If he props up his house, it will not stand, And when he takes hold of it, it will not endure.
8.16: For it is moist under the sun, And his branch shall come forth out of his rottenness.
8.17: He shall lie down upon a pile of rocks And shall live in the midst of flints.
8.18: If he is swallowed up, his place shall deny him. You have not seen such things,
8.19: “That such is the destruction of the ungodly, And out of the earth another will grow up again.
8.20: For the Lord will not cast off the innocent, Nor will He accept any gift of an ungodly man.
8.21: He will fill the mouth of the true with laughter And their lips with thanksgiving.
8.22: But their enemies will be clothed with shame, And the dwelling of an ungodly man will be no more.” Job Has No Mediator

9.2: “I know that is true, But how can a mortal man be righteous before the Lord?
9.3: If he should wish to enter into judgment with Him, The Lord would not listen to him, For he could not answer to one out of a thousand of His charges.
9.4: He is wise in mind and mighty and great. Who has hardened him self against Him and endured?
9.5: He who makes the mountains old, and men do not know it; He who overturns them in His wrath;
9.6: He who shakes the earth under heaven from its foundations, And its pillars tremble;
9.7: He who commands the sun, and it does not rise; He who seals off the stars;
9.8: He who alone stretches out heaven; He who walks on the sea as on firm ground;
9.9: He who makes Pleiades, Hesperus, and Arcturus, And the chambers of the south;
9.10: He who does great and unsearchable things, Glorious and marvelous things without number.
9.11: If He goes beyond me, I do not see Him; If He passes by me, I do not perceive Him;
9.12: If He takes away, who can turn Him back? Who can say to Him, ‘What have You done?’
9.13: For if He turns away His wrath, The great sea creatures under heaven lie prostrate beneath Him.
9.14: “Would then that He would hear me, or judge my words.
9.15: For though I be righteous, He will not listen to me. I will entreat His judgment.
9.16: If I should call, and He hears me, I would not believe He is listening to me.
9.17: Let Him not destroy me with darkness, But He has caused my great destruction to no purpose.
9.18: For He will not allow me to draw breath, But has filled me with bitterness.
9.19: For if He is strong in power, Who then can resist His judgment?
9.20: For though I were righteous, my mouth will be impious; And though I were blameless, I will be perverse.
9.21: “If I am ungodly, I do not know it in my soul, But my life is taken away.
9.22: Therefore I said, ‘Wrath destroys the great and the mighty.’
9.23: The wrongdoers die violently, But the righteous are laughed to scorn.
9.24: For they are delivered into the hands of the ungodly man. He covers the faces of the judges of the earth. If it is not He, who else could it be?
9.25: “Now my life passes swifter than a runner; My days have fled away, and they do not see it.
9.26: Do the ships leave a mark of their path? Or does a flying eagle leave a trace of its soaring as it seeks its prey?
9.27: If I say, ‘I will forget to speak,’ I will bow down my face and groan.
9.28: I shake with fear in all my limbs; I know You will not leave me as innocent.
9.29: But since I am ungodly, why have I not died?
9.30: If I should wash myself with snow And cleanse myself with pure hands,
9.31: You have fully immersed me in filth, And my garment detests me.
9.32: “For You are not a man, as I am, With whom I could contend, That we should go to judgment together.
9.33: Would that we had a mediator who would cross-exam ine And hear the case between us.
9.34: Let Him remove the rod from me, And do not let the fear of Him distress me.
9.35: Then I will not be afraid, but will speak, For I am not conscious of any guilt.

10.1: Lord, Why Have You Judged Me? “Since I am weary and groaning in my soul, I will let loose my words to Him. Because I am distressed, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
10.2: I will say to the Lord, ‘Do not teach me to be ungodly. Why have You thus judged me?
10.3: Is it good before You if I do wrong, And that You renounce the work of Your hands, And give heed to the counsel of the ungodly?
10.4: Do You see as the mortal sees? Do You see as man sees?
10.5: Is Your life human life? Are Your years like the years of a man,
10.6: That You examined my lawlessness And searched out my sins?
10.7: You know I have not acted impiously, But who is he who can deliver from Your hands?
10.8: ‘Your hands fashioned and made me; Then You changed Your mind and struck me.
10.9: Remember that You fashioned me as clay, But You are turning me back to earth again.
10.10: Did You not squeeze me out like milk And curdle me like cheese?
10.11: You clothed me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews.
10.12: You granted me life and mercy, And Your visitation has guarded my spirit.
10.13: ‘Since You have these things in Yourself, I know You are able to do all things; For nothing is impossible for You.
10.14: For if I sin, You watch me; And because of my lawlessness You will not consider me innocent.
10.15: For if I am ungodly, woe to me, And if I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head; For I am full of dishonor.
10.16: I am trapped like a lion for slaughter; For again You have changed, and You are destroying me.
10.17: You renewed my affliction upon me, And dealt with me in great wrath; For You brought severe ordeals upon me.
10.18: ‘Why then did You bring me out of the womb? Why did I not die, and no eye see me?
10.19: Why have I become as though I had not been? For why was I not carried from the womb to the grave?
10.20: Is not the time of my life short? Allow me to rest a little
10.21: Before I go to the place from which I shall not return, To an obscure and dark land,
10.22: To a land of eternal darkness, where there is no light, Neither can anyone see the life of m ortals.’ ” Job Rebuked by Zophar

11.1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
11.2: “He who speaks much should also listen in turn, Or does the fluent speaker think him self to be righteous? Blessed is the short-liv ed offspring of a woman.
11.3: Do not be wordy in your speech, For there is no one to reply to you.
11.4: Do not say, ‘I am pure in my works And blameless before Him.’
11.5: But how does the Lord speak to you? He will open His lips against you.
11.6: Then He will declare to you the power of wisdom, For it shall be double in your case. At that time you will know a worthy recompense Has come to you from the Lord because of your sins.
11.7: Will you find the traces of the Lord? Have you reached the outer extrem ities Of what the Almighty has made?
11.8: Heaven is high, and what will you do? And what do you know, For there are even deeper things in Hades?
11.9: Do you know those dim ensions That are longer than the earth and broader than the sea?
11.10: If He should overthrow everything, Who then will say to Him, ‘What have You done?’
11.11: For He knows the works of the lawless; And when He sees wrongs, He shall not overlook them.
11.12: But man vainly swims in words, And a mortal born of a woman is equal to a donkey in the desert.
11.13: If you have made your heart pure And stretch out your hands toward Him,
11.14: If something lawless is done by your hands, Put it far away from you; And do not let any wrongdoing lodge in your dwelling.
11.15: For in this way, your face will shine forth like pure water, For you will cleanse away the filth. You will not fear.
11.16: Then you will forget this hardship Like a wave that has passed away; And you will not be terrified.
11.17: Your prayer will be like the morning star. At midday, life will rise to you.
11.18: You will be confident because you have hope; And peace shall bring light to you out of anxiety and care.
11.19: You will also be at rest, And there will be no one to fight against you. Many will change their mind about you and supplicate you.
11.20: But salvation will forsake them, for their hope will be lost, And the eyes of the ungodly will melt away.” Job Chides His Critics

12.2: “Moreov er you are men. Surely wisdom will die with you?
12.3: But I also have a heart as well as you.
12.4: “A righteous and blameless man Has become an object of mockery.
12.5: For it had been ordained that he should fall Under the power of others at the appointed time, And his houses should be plundered by the lawless.
12.6: Let not, however, anyone be persuaded That, if he is evil, he will be held innocent. Let not those who provoke the Lord Be persuaded there will be no trial for them.
12.7: “But now ask the four-footed animals if they may speak to you, And the birds of the air if they may report it to you.
12.8: Tell the earth if it may interpret it to you, And the fish of the sea will explain to you.
12.9: Who am ong all these does not know The hand of the Lord created them,
12.10: That in His hand is the life of every living thing, And the breath of every man?
12.11: For indeed, the ear discerns words, And the palate tastes wheat.
12.12: In length of time is wisdom, And in long life, knowledge.

By the late first century BC, as seen in the Wisdom of Solomon, immortality is directly linked with living in wisdom and righteousness: “Kinship with Wisdom is immortality” (WSol 8:17); “The righteous shall live forever” (WSol 5:15; see also 1:13–15; 2:22, 23; 6:17– 21). Various passages from this book (WSol 3:1–9; 4:7–15; 5:15—6:3) are read at Vespers in commemoration of some of the more prominent saints. At the time of Christ, the Sadducees rejected belief in an afterlife (see Mt 22:23), while the Pharisees did believe in resurrection and immortality (Acts 23:6–8). It was the Pharisees’ view which came to dominate in later Judaism. Lazarus’ sister Martha knew about a general “resurrection at the last day” (Jn 11:24), but Jesus declares to her that resurrection and eternal life come only through Him (Jn 11:25; see 3:14–16; 4:14; 6:40, 47–58; 14:1–6). Christ promises that believers will be with Him after their death (Lk 23:42, 43; see
15.2: Co 5:8; Php 1:21–23). The souls of believers are further enlightened in Christ, as they experience a foretaste of the eternal heavenly kingdom. Yet all the departed still await the general resurrection, the day when their souls will be reunited with their bodies, which are transformed into a glorified state (1Co 15:50–54) like Christ’s own body (Php 3:20, 21; 1Jn 3:2). 24.3: They have led away the donkey of the orphans And have taken the widow's ox as a pledge.
24.4: They have turned aside the weak from the right way; The gentle of the land have hidden themselves together.
24.5: They departed like donkeys in the field. Contrary to me, they went forth to their own pursuits. Their bread was sweet to their little ones.
24.6: For they harvested a field that was not their own before the time, And the weak worked the vineyard of the ungodly Without pay or food.
24.7: They caused many naked to sleep without clothing, And they took away the covering of their life.
24.8: They are wet with the showers of the mountains And have huddled around the rock for want of shelter.
24.9: Theyhavesnatched the orphan from the breast And have humiliated the banished.
24.10: They have unjustly caused them to sleep without clothing, And they have taken away the morsel from the hungry.
24.11: They have wrongfully laid snares in narrow places And have not known the way of righteousness.
24.12: They have cast the weak out of the city and their own houses, And the soul of the infants sighed greatly. Why then has He not visited them?
24.13: “They are ones on the earth who do not know the Lord, And they do not understand the way of righteousness, Nor do they walk in His paths.
24.14: But He knows their works and delivered them into darkness; And one shall be like a thief in the night.
24.15: For the eye of the adulterer watches for the darkness, Saying, ‘No eye will perceive me’; And he puts a covering on his face.
24.16: In the dark he breaks into houses; In the daytime they seal themselves up; They do not know the light.
24.17: For in due time, the shadow of death will be the same to them, Because they shall know the troubles of the shadow of death.
24.18: “He is swift on the face of the waters; May his portion be cursed on earth.
24.19: May their plants wither on earth, For they have taken away from the orphans Even the smallest portions.
24.20: Then his sin is recalled to memory, And he vanishes like a mist of dew; But what he has done, may it be recompensed to him, And may every wrongdoer be crushed like rotten wood.
24.21: For he has not treated the barren woman well, And showed no mercy to the feeble woman.
24.22: “In his anger, he overturns the weak; Therefore when he rises up, No one believes his own life is safe.
24.23: When he falls sick, let him not hope to recover, But let him perish by disease.
24.24: For his exaltation mistreated many, But he has withered as m allows in the heat, Or as an ear of corn falling on its own from the stalk.
24.25: “If it is not so, who says I speak falsely And will make my speech worth nothing?” Bildad Asks How Man Can Be Righteous

25.1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
25.2: “What beginning or fear is His— He who makes all things in the highest heaven?
25.3: For may no one imagine there is a respite for pirates. Upon whom will there not be an am bush from Him?
25.4: How shall a mortal be righteous before the Lord? Or how may he who is born of a woman purify himself?
25.5: If He orders the moon, then it does not shine, And the stars are not pure in His sight.
25.6: But alas! Man is putrid, and the son of man a worm.” God Is All Powerful

26.2: “To whom are you attached, Or whom are you going to help? Is it not He who has great strength And whose arm is powerful?
26.3: To whom have you given counsel? Is it not to Him who has all wisdom? Or whom will you follow? Is it not One who has the greatest power?
26.4: To whom have you spoken words? Whose breath came forth from you?
26.5: “Will giants be born under the water And those inhabiting them?
26.6: Hades is naked before Him, And destruction has no covering.
26.7: He stretches out the north wind upon nothing; He hangs the earth on nothing.
26.8: He binds up the water in His clouds, Yet the cloud is not broken under it.
26.9: He grasps the face of His throne And spreads His cloud over it.
26.10: He encom passed the face of the water by an ordinance Until the end of light and darkness.
26.11: The pillars of heaven were spread all over And stood am azed at His rebuke.
26.12: He checked the sea with His power, And by His understanding He wounded the sea-m onster.
26.13: For the bars of heaven fear Him, Because He put to death the rebellious dragon bya command.
26.14: Behold, these are parts of His way, And we will hearken to the least of His words. But who knows when He will bring about the strength of His thunder?” Job Will Hold Fast to Righteousness

27.1: Moreover Job continued his speech and said:
27.2: “As the Lord lives who thus judges me, And the Almighty who embittered my soul,
27.3: Surely as long as my breath is in me And the divine breath is in my nostrils,
27.4: My lips will not speak lawless things, Nor shall my soul practice wrongdoings.
27.5: May it not be I who set forth the opinion that you are righteous. Until the day I die, I will not put away my integrity from me.
27.6: I hold fast to my righteousness and am not letting it go; For I am not conscious in myself of having done anything wrong.
27.7: “Surely not, but rather may my enemies Be as the destruction of the ungodly, And those who rise up against me As the destruction of the lawless.
27.8: For what hope is there for an ungodly man that he holds to it? Will he trust in the Lord and be saved?
27.9: Will the Lord hear his pray er When distress comes upon him?
27.10: Has he any confidence before Him, Or will the Lord hear him when he calls on Him?
27.11: “But indeed, I will tell you what is the hand of the Lord. I will not lie concerning what is with the Almighty.
27.12: Behold therefore, all of you know You are adding vanity to vanity.
27.13: “This is the portion from the Lord for the ungodly man, And the possession of oppressors Shall come upon them from the Almighty.
27.14: If their children be many, they will be for slaughter; And if they reach manhood, they will beg.
27.15: Those who survive him shall be buried in death, And no one will have pity on their widows.
27.16: Though he gathers silver like dust And shall prepare gold like clay,
27.17: The righteous will acquire these things, And the true ones will possess his wealth.
27.18: His house goes away like a moth And like a spider's web.
27.19: The rich man will lie down and not continue; He opens his eyes, but is no more.
27.20: Pains happen to him like a flood, And thick darkness takes him away in the night.
27.21: A burning wind will take him up, and he will be gone; And it will scatter him from his place.
27.22: It will blow against him and not spare; He will try in vain to flee from its force.
27.23: It will strike him with its power, And whistle him from his place.

28.1: The Richness of the Earth “Indeed, there is a place for silver, from whence it comes, And a place for gold, from whence it is refined.
28.2: Certainly, iron is taken from the earth, And copper is hewn out like a stone.
28.3: He set an order to darkness And examines accurately every limit. A stone is darkness and the shadow of death.
28.4: There is a narrow channel of the brook because of dust; So those who forget the right way Are weakened because of mortal men.
28.5: As for the earth, from it will come bread, But underneath, it is turned up as by fire;
28.6: Its stones are the source of sapphires, And its dust contains gold.
28.7: There is a path no bird knows, Nor has the eye of a vulture seen it.
28.8: The sons of the arrogant have not trodden it, Nor has the lion passed over it.
28.9: He has stretched forth his hand to quarry stones And has overturned the mountains by the roots.
28.10: He has broken asunder the whirlpools of rivers, And my eye has seen every valued thing.
28.11: He has uncovered the depths of the rivers And has brought his power to light. > Where Is Wisdom Found?
28.12: “But where can wisdom be found? What is the place of understanding?
28.13: Mortal man has not known its way, Nor is it found among men.
28.14: The deep said, ‘It is not in me’; And the sea said, ‘It is not with me.’
28.15: One shall not give massive piles of gold instead of it, Nor can silver be weighed in exchange for it.
28.16: It cannot be compared with the gold of Ophir, With the precious onyx or sapphire.
28.17: Neither gold nor crystal will equal it, Nor can it be exchanged for vessels of gold.
28.18: No mention shall be made of coral and quartz, But you must hold up wisdom above the most valued things.
28.19: The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, Nor can it be compared with pure gold.
28.20: “From where then is wisdom found, And what is the place of understanding?
28.21: It has been hidden from every man And concealed from the birds of the sky.
28.22: Destruction and Death said, ‘We have heard about its fame.’
28.23: God has well established its way, And He knows its place.
28.24: For He watches over the whole earth under heaven, Knowing the things in the earth, all He has made—
28.25: The weight of the winds and the measures of the water.
28.26: When He made them, He numbered them And made a way for the claps of thunder.
28.27: Then He saw wisdom and declared it; He prepared it and traced it out.

29.1: He said to man, ‘behold, the fear of God is wisdom, And to abstain from evils is understanding.’” The Glories of the Past 29
29.2: Job continued further and said in his speech: “Who may put me in months past, As in the days when God protected me—
29.3: As when His lampshone upon my head, And by His light I walked in the darkness;
29.4: As when I steadfast ly pursued my ways, When God's visitation was over my house;
29.5: As when I lived in abundance, And my children were around me;
29.6: As when my roads spread out with butter, And the mountains flowed with milk for me;
29.7: “As when I went early in the city, And took my seat in the open square;
29.8: The young men saw me and hid, And all the old men stood up.
29.9: The great men refrained from talking And put their finger to their mouth.
29.10: Those who heard me blessed me, And their tongue stuck to their throat.
29.11: The ear heard and blessed me, And the eye saw me and turned aside.
29.12: For I saved the poor from the hand of the oppressor And helped the orphan who had no helper.
29.13: The blessing of the perishing man came upon me, And the widow's mouth blessed me.
29.14: I put on righteousness And clothed myself with judgment like a robe.
29.15: I was the eye of the blind and the foot of the lame.
29.16: I was the father of the weak, And I searched out the cause I did not know.
29.17: I broke the molars of the wrongdoers And plucked the spoil from the midst of their teeth.
29.18: “Then I said, ‘My age shall continue as the stem of a palm tree, And I shall live a long while.’
29.19: My root was spread out to the waters, And the dew would settle on my harvest.
29.20: My glory was fresh within me, And my bow prospered in its hand.
29.21: “Men heard and listened to me And kept silence for my counsel.
29.22: At my word they did not speak again, And they were very glad when I spoke to them.
29.23: They waited for my speech As the thirsty earth for the rain.
29.24: If I laughed at them, they did not believe it, And the light of my countenance did not fail.
29.25: I chose the way for them and sat as a ruler; And I dwelt as a king in the army, As one who comforts mourners.

30.1: The Present Seems Futile “But now they laugh me to scorn, Men younger than I, whose fathers I disdained; Whom I did not deem worthy to be put With the dogs of my pastures.
30.2: Indeed, what profit is the strength of their hands to me? For them the full term of life was lost.
30.3: In want and famine, they are childless. Yesterday they fled to a waterless desert in anguish and misery.
30.4: They are those who surround the noisy salt places, Who havesaltyherbs for their food, And who are also considered worthless And deficient of every good thing, And chew on the roots of trees because of their great hunger.
30.5: Thieves have risen up against me,
30.6: Whose houses were holes in the rocks,
30.7: Who cry out among the rustling bushes And live under the wild shrubs.
30.8: They are the sons of fools and dishonored men, Whose name and fame were extinguished from the earth.
30.9: “But now I am their lyre, And they have me as their by word.
30.10: They detest me and keep their distance. They do not hesitate to spit in my face.
30.11: For He has opened His quiver and afflicted me. They have cast off restraint in my presence.
30.12: They rose up against me by the right hands of their offspring; And they stretched out their foot And directed against me their paths of destruction.
30.13: My paths are ruined, for they stripped off my garment.
30.14: He shot me down with His arrows And used me as He wished. I am overwhelmed with pains.
30.15: My pains are turned upon me. My hope is gone like the wind And my salvation like a cloud.
30.16: “Ev en now my soul will be poured forth upon me, And the days of pains seize me.
30.17: By night my bones are set on fire, And my sinews are broken up.
30.18: With great force He took hold of my garment, And like the collar of my tunic He surrounded me.
30.19: You regarded me as clay in the earth, And my portion is with ashes.
30.20: “I cry out to You, but You do not answer me. They stood and observed me.
30.21: You attacked me without mercy And scourged me with a strong hand.
30.22: You appointed pains for me And cast me away from salvation.
30.23: For I know death will destroy me, For the earth is the house for every mortal.
30.24: “Would that I might lay hands on myself, Or at least ask another, and he would do it for me.
30.25: Yet I wept over every man without strength And groaned when I sawa man in distress.
30.26: But while I held firm ly to good things, Days of evils happened to me instead.
30.27: My stomach churns and will not be quiet, And days of poverty have come upon me.
30.28: I go groaning without restraint; I stand up and cry out in the church.
30.29: I have become a brother of sirens And a companion of sparrows.
30.30: My skin has been greatly darkened, And my bones are burned by the heat.
30.31: My lyre turned into mourning And my song into my weeping.

31.1: Job Sets Forth His Integrity “I have made a covenant with my eyes, And I will not think upon a virgin.
31.2: What has God apportioned from above, And what is the inheritance of the Mighty One from on high?
31.3: Is not destruction for the wrongdoer, And alienation for those who do lawlessness?
31.4: Will He not see my way and count all my steps?
31.5: “If I have walked with scorners, Or if my foot has hastened to deceit,
31.6: May He weigh me therefore with a just scale, For He knows my integrity.
31.7: If my foot has turned from the way, Or if my heart has followed after my eyes, Or if gifts have touched my hands,
31.8: Then may I sow and others eat. Yes, may I be uprooted on the earth.
31.9: “If my heart has followed after another m an's wife, Or if I have laid wait at her door,
31.10: Then also may my wife please another, And may my children be humiliated.
31.11: For the rage of anger is uncontrollable In defiling another m an's wife.
31.12: For it is a fire burning on every side, And whomever it comes upon, it destroys at the roots.
31.13: If I have despised the judgment of my servant or handmaid When they judged me,
31.14: What then will I do when the Lord brings me to trial and visits me? How shall I answer Him?
31.15: Did not He who made me in the womb make them? So we were fashioned in the same womb.
31.16: “But the weak did not miss whatever they happened to need, And I did not cause the eyes of the widow to fail.
31.17: If I ate mymorsel by myself And did not share it with the orphan
31.18: (But from my youth I nourished them as a father, And from mym other's womb I guided the widow);
31.19: If I have neglected the naked as he was perishing And did not clothe him;
31.20: If the weak did not bless me, And if their shoulders were not warmed with the fleece of my lambs;
31.21: If I raised my hand against the orphan, Trusting that my strength was far superior to his,
31.22: Then let my shoulder fall from my collarbone; Let my arm be torn from its socket.
31.23: For the fear of the Lord seized me, And I cannot endure His burden.
31.24: If I have made gold my strength Or trusted the precious stone,
31.25: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And if I, too, laid my hand on countless treasures
31.26: (Or do I not see the shining sun eclipsed and the moon waning? For this does not depend upon them );
31.27: If my heart has been secretly deceived, And if I have laid my hand upon my mouth and kissed it,
31.28: Then may this also be reckoned to me As the greatest lawlessness; For I have lied against the Lord most high.
31.29: “If I, too, was glad at the fall of my enemies, And my heart said, ‘Good! Well done!’
31.30: Then may my ear hear my curse, And may I be a by word among my people in my affliction.
31.31: If my handmaids have often said, ‘Who may give us his meat to be satisfied?’ (But I was very kind.
31.32: For the stranger did not spend the night outside; And my door was opened to everyone who came);
31.33: If I sinned in voluntarily, then covered my sin,
31.34: (For I did not stand in awe of great multitude, So as not to confess before them ); And if I permitted a poor man to go out of my door With an empty bosom
31.35: (Who may listen to me?); And if I had not feared the hand of the Lord, And as to the document I had against someone,
31.36: I would place it as a crown on my shoulders and read it,
31.37: And if I did not tear it up and return it, Having taken nothing from the debtor;
31.38: “If at anytime the land groaned against me And its furrows wept together,
31.39: If I have eaten its strength alone without paying, Or if I also grieved the soul of the owner of the land By casting him out,

32.1: Then may the nettle come to me instead of wheat, And bramble instead of barley.” Thus Job ceased speaking. Elihu Is Angered at Job and His Friends 32 Job's three friends also ceased answering him, for he was righteous before them.
32.2: Then Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, of the country of Ausitis, became furious; and he was very angry with Job, because he declared himself to be righteous before the Lord.
32.3: He was also very angry with Job's three friends, because they found no answer to Job, and yet affirmed he was an ungodly man.
32.4: Now because they were years older than he, Elihu waited to speak to Job.
32.5: So when Elihu saw there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was aroused.
32.6: So Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: “I am young in years, and you are the elder; Therefore I was silent And dared not declare my knowledge to you.
32.7: I said, ‘It is not time that speaks, Though in many years, men know wisdom.’
32.8: But there is a spirit in m ortals, And the breath of the Almighty is that which teaches them.
32.9: The long-liv ed are not always wise, Nor do the old men always know judgment.
32.10: “Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me, I also will declare what I know.’
32.11: Pay close attention to my words, For I will speak in your hearing, while you examine my words,
32.12: And until I shall understand you. So behold, not one of you answered Job in argument;
32.13: Lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom added to the Lord.’
32.14: But you permitted a man to speak such words.
32.15: “They were dismayed and answered no more; They made their words obsolete.
32.16: I waited, for they did not speak. Because they stood still, they did not answer.”
32.18: ‘Again I will speak, for I am full of words; The spirit within my stomach is killing me.
32.19: Indeed, my stomach is like a wineskin of sweet new wine, Bound up and ready to burst, Or like the blowpipe of a coppersmith, ready to bellow.
32.20: I will speak, that I may find relief in opening my lips.
32.21: I will not feel shame before any man, Neither indeed will I feel shame before any mortal.
32.22: For I do not know how to flatter persons, Or else the moths would eat me.

33.1: Elihu Claims He Speaks for God “Nev ertheless, hear my words, Job, And pay close attention to what I say.
33.2: For behold, I have opened my mouth And my tongue has spoken.
33.3: By my words, my heart shall be found pure; And the understanding of my lips will think pure thoughts.
33.4: The divine Spirit has made me, And the breath of the Almighty is that which teaches me.
33.5: Give mean answer to these things if you can. Endure and stand firm against me, and I against you.
33.6: You and I were formed out of the clay; Thus, we have been formed out of the same substance.
33.7: My fear will not distract you, Neither shall my hand be heavy on you.
33.8: “Howev er you said in my hearing (I heard the voice of your words),
33.9: For you say, ‘I am pure, for I have not sinned. I am blameless, for I have not acted lawlessly.
33.10: Yet He has found a charge against me; He has counted me as His enemy.
33.11: He has put my feet in the stocks, And He watches all my paths.’
33.12: “For how can you say, ‘I am righteous, yet He has not listened to me’? For He that is above m ortals is eternal.
33.13: But you say, ‘Why has He not heard every word of my cause?’
33.14: For when the Lord speaks once, Or in another time in a dream,
33.15: Or in a m editation of the night (As when dreadful fear falls upon men While slumbering on their bed),
33.16: Then He unveils the hearts of men And frightens them with such fearful visions
33.17: So as to turn man from his wrongdoing; Thus He delivers his body froma fall.
33.18: He keeps back his soul from death And does not allow him to fall in war.
33.19: “Again He also chastens him with sickness on his bed, And the multitude of his bones grownumb.
33.20: He is not able to receive any food, Though his soul may long for it,
33.21: Until his flesh wastes away And he shows his bones bare.
33.22: His soul also draws near to death And his life to Hades.
33.23: “If there are a thousand death-bringing messengers, None of them shall wound him. If he purposes in his heart to turn to the Lord, And declares to man his fault, and shows his folly,
33.24: He will support him, that he might not fall into death; And He will renew his body like fresh plaster upon a wall, And fill his bones with marrow.
33.25: He will make his flesh young like a child's And restore him among men in full manhood.
33.26: He shall pray to the Lord, and his pray er shall be accepted. He shall come to prayer with an innocent face And with an utterance of thanksgiving, For He will restore righteousness to men.
33.27: Even then, a man shall blame himself, saying, ‘I am to blame because of what I did, Yet He has not examined my guilt To the extent of my unworthiness.’
33.28: Save my soul from going down to corruption, So my life shall see the light.
33.29: “Behold all these things: The Mighty One works three ways with a man.
33.30: But He has delivered my soul from death That my life may praise Him in the light.
33.31: “Giv eear, Job; listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will speak.
33.32: If you have anything to say, answer me; Speak, for I desire you to be declared as righteous.

34.1: If not, listen to me; Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.” Elihu Proclaims God's Justice 34
34.2: Elihu continued and said: “Hear me, O wise men who are present, And pay close attention to what is good.
34.3: For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
34.4: Let us choose judgment for ourselves; Let us know among ourselves what is good.
34.5: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, And the Lord has taken away my judgment.’
34.6: But he spoke untruth in my judgment when he said, ‘My wound is severe, though I am without wrongdoing.’
34.7: What man is like Job, Who drinks scorn like water?
34.8: For he says, ‘I have not sinned, nor committed ungodliness, Nor had anything in common with the workers of lawlessness, So as to walk with ungodly men.’
34.9: For you should not say, ‘There shall be no visitation of a man,’ Whereas there is a visitation on him from the Lord.
34.10: “Therefore listen to me, you wise in heart: May it be far from me to act in an ungodly way before the Lord And to pervert righteousness before the Almighty.
34.11: Yes, He renders to a man as each one of them does, And in a m an's path He will find him.
34.12: Do you think the Lord will do wrong, Or will the Almighty who made the earth pervert judgment?
34.13: Who is He who created everything under heaven And all things therein?
34.14: If He should wish to hold and restrain His breath within Him self,
34.15: All flesh would die together, And every mortal would return to the ground From which he was form ed.
34.16: Take heed to this, lest He warn you; Pay close attention to the voice of His words.
34.17: Behold then the one who hates lawless things And destroys the evil ones. He is forever righteous.
34.18: He is ungodly who says to a king, ‘You act contrary to the law,’ And to rulers, ‘O, most ungodly one.’
34.19: Such a man is not ashamed Before the face of an honorable man, Nor does he know how to give honor to the great, So as to show proper respect.
34.20: But it will prove to be in vain for them to cry out And beg the favor of a man; For they dealt unlawfully when they turned aside the weak.
34.21: “For He is the observer of the works of man, And nothing of what they do escapes Him.
34.22: There is no place for the workers of lawlessness to hide themselves.
34.23: He need not further consider a man, For the Lord gazes upon all men.
34.24: He comprehends unsearchable things, Glorious also and extraordinary things without number.
34.25: He discloses their works; And He will overthrow them in the night, And they will be brought low.
34.26: He extinguishes the ungodly, For they are visible before Him,
34.27: Because they turned aside from the law of God And would not regard His ordinances,
34.28: So as to bring before Him the cry of the needy; For He will hear the cry of the poor.
34.29: He will provide quietness, and who shall condemn Him? And He will hide His face, and who shall see Him? Whether it be done against a nation or a man jointly,
34.30: To cause a hypocrite to be king, Because of the discontent of the people.
34.31: “For there is one that says to the Mighty One, ‘I have received blessings; I will not take in pledge;
34.32: I will see apart from myself; Show me if I have done unrighteousness, And I will do so no more.’
34.33: Will He not take vengeance for it from you, Because you failed to listen to your conscience? For you will choose, and not I; Therefore, speak what you know. Elihu Rebukes Job Sternly
34.34: “For this reason wise men in heart shall say this, And a wise man listens to my word.
34.35: But Job has spoken without understanding, And his words are without knowledge.
34.36: But learn, Job, and no longer answer like that of foolish men,
34.37: That we add not to our sins; For lawlessness will be counted against us If we speak many words against the Lord.”

35.2: “What is this you consider as judgment? Who are you to say, ‘I am righteous before the Lord’?
35.3: Or will you say, ‘What did I do, if I have sinned?’
35.4: “I will answer you and your three friends.
35.5: Look up to heaven and see, And observe the cloud as higher than you.
35.6: If you have sinned, what will you do? If you have acted very lawlessly, what can you do?
35.7: Since therefore you are righteous, what will you give Him? Or what did He receive from your hand?
35.8: Your ungodliness mayaffect a man such as you, Or your righteousness a son of man.
35.9: “Those who are slandered bya multitude will cry out; They will cry out for help because of the strength of the many.
35.10: But no one says, ‘Where is the God who made me, Who appoints the night watches,
35.11: Who distinguishes me from the four-footed animals of the earth And from the birds of heaven?’
35.12: There they will cry out, but no one answers, Because of the insolence of evil men.
35.13: For the Lord does not desire to look on wrongdoing,
35.14: For He, the Almighty, is the observer Of those who perform lawless deeds, But He will save me. Decide before Him if you can praise Him as it is now possible.
35.15: But now, He is not v isiting His wrath, Nor even taking notice of very much transgression;
35.16: Yet Job opens his mouth in vain; In ignorance he burdens us with words.” Elihu Upholds God's Goodness

36.2: ‘Wait for me yet a little while, that I may teach you, For there is yet more for me to say.
36.3: I will gather my knowledge from afar And truly speak of righteousness in my works.
36.4: You were not hearing unjust words without good reason.
36.5: “But know that the Lord who is mighty in strength of heart Does not cast off an innocent man.
36.6: He will not give life to the ungodly, But He will give judgment to the poor.
36.7: He will not turn away from the righteous, But will seat them on the throne with kings; For He will lift them in triumph, and they will be exalted.
36.8: But if they are bound in fetters, They shall be held in the cords of poverty.
36.9: He will tell them their works and their transgressions, For such will act with violence.
36.10: He also will hear the righteous, And He said they will turn from wrongdoing.
36.11: If they give ear and serve Him, They shall spend their days in good things And their years in dignity.
36.12: But He does not save the ungodly, Because they are not willing to know the Lord, And because they refused to listen when they were admonished.
36.13: “For the hypocrites in heart will marshal anger against themselves, And they will not cry for help, because He has bound them.
36.14: Therefore, may their soul die in youth, And their life be wounded by messengers of death,
36.15: Because they afflicted the weak and helpless; And He will make manifest the judgment of the gentle.
36.16: “Besides, He deceived you by the mouth of the enemy. There is an abyss and a pouring over beneath it, And your table descended full of fatness.
36.17: Judgment shall not fail from the righteous,
36.18: But there shall be anger against the ungodly Because of the ungodliness of the gifts they received for wrongdoings.
36.19: Let not your heart willingly turn you aside From the petition of the weak who are in distress.
36.20: Do not lure away all the mighty men at night So the people should go up instead of them.
36.21: “But guard yourself, lest you do what is wrong, For you chose this because of poverty.
36.22: Behold, the Mighty One shall prevail by His strength. Who is so powerful as He?
36.23: Who is he who examines His works? Or who can say, ‘He has done unjustly ’? God's Works Are Great
36.24: “Rem ember, His works are great, Because of which men began to exist.
36.25: Everyone has seen for himself Howmanymortals are wounded.
36.26: “Behold, the Mighty One is great, And we do not know Him. The number of His years is also endless.
36.27: For He numbers the drops of rain, And they shall be poured out in rain to form a cloud.
36.28: The ancient clouds shall drop down And over shadow in num er able m ortals. He has fixed a time for cattle, And they know the appointed time for their rest. Yet your mind is not astonished by these things, Nor does your heart leap out from your body.
36.29: For one should perceive the outspreadings of a cloud And the measure of His tabernacle.
36.30: Behold, He stretches His bow against him And covers the bottom of the sea.
36.31: For by these He will judge the peoples. He will give food to him who has strength.
36.32: He has hidden light in His hands And given orders to the cloud by which it is diverted.
36.33: The Lord will proclaim it to His friend, But there is also a portion for unrighteousness.

37.1: “At this also my heart was troubled and flows from its place.
37.2: Listen attentively to the thunder of the Lord's wrath And the discourse coming from His mouth.
37.3: His dominion is under the whole heaven And His light to the ends of the earth.
37.4: Behind Him a voice will cry aloud. He will thunder with His voice of outrage, Yet He will not change them when His voice is heard.
37.5: The Mighty One will thunder marvelouslywith His voice, For He does great things we cannot comprehend.
37.6: For He commands the snow, ‘Fall upon the earth,’ And likewise there is the winter, The rain and the winter storms of His might.
37.7: He seals up the hand of every man That everyone may know his weakness.
37.8: The wild animals go into their shelters And are at rest in their lairs.
37.9: From the secret chambers comes the whirlwind, And cold from the mountaintop.
37.10: By the breath of the Mighty One, He will send frost, And He freezes the waters as He wishes.
37.11: And when the cloud obscures what He chooses, His light will disperse the cloud.
37.12: He will swirl the encircling clouds by His gov ernance To perform all their works, Moving them to do whatever He commands. This has been appointed by Him on the earth,
37.13: Whether for correction or for His earth, Or if He shall find him an object for mercy.
37.14: “Pay close attention to this, O Job. Stand still and consider the power of the Lord.
37.15: We know that God has appointed His works, Having made light out of darkness.
37.16: He knows the division of the clouds And the violent falls of evil men.
37.17: But your robe is warm, And there is quiet upon the land.
37.18: Will you establish with Him the foundations For the ancient heavens? They are strong like a molten mirror.
37.19: “What is this to you? Teach me what we will say to Him, And let us cease speaking many words.
37.20: Have I a book or scribe by me That I may stand and put man to silence?
37.21: But the light is not visible to all. It shines far off in the ancient heavens, As that which is from Him in the clouds.
37.22: From the north come the clouds, shining like gold; In these great things are the glory and honor of the Almighty.
37.23: We do not find another like Him in His strength. Do you not think He who judges righteously listens?
37.24: Therefore men shall fear Him, And the wise in heart shall fear Him.” The Lord Speaks to Job

38.1: After Elihu had ceased from speaking, then the Lord spoke to Job out of the whirlwind and clouds, saying:
38.2: “Who is this who hides counsel from Me, And holds words in his heart And thinks to conceal them from Me?
38.3: Gird your waist like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer Me. The Majestic Creator
38.4: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
38.5: Who determined its measurements? Surely you know. Or who stretched the line upon it?
38.6: To what were its foundations fastened, Or who laid its cornerstone,
38.7: When the stars were made And all My angels praised Me in a loud voice?
38.8: “I shut up the sea with doors When it burst forth and issued from the womb.
38.9: I made the clouds its garment and wrapped it in mist.
38.10: I fixed My limit for it and set bars and doors.
38.11: I said, ‘This far you may come, but no further, And here your waves must stop.’
38.12: “Did I order the morning light in your time, And did the morning star see its appointed place,
38.13: To lay hold of the ends of the earth And to shake the ungodly out of it?
38.14: Or did you take clay of the ground and form a living creature, And set it with the power of speech upon the earth?
38.15: Have you removed light from the ungodly And crushed the arm of the arrogant?
38.16: “Hav e you come upon the fountain of the sea And walked in the tracks of the deep?
38.17: Do the gates of death open to you for fear, And did the doorkeepers of Hades quake when they saw you?
38.18: Have you been instructed in the breadth of the earth under heaven? Tell Me now, what is the extent of it?
38.19: “In what kind of land does the light dwell, And what kind is the place of darkness?
38.20: If you would bring Me to their boundaries, And also if you understand their paths,
38.21: Then I know you were born at that time, And the number of your years is great.
38.22: “Hav e you come upon the storehouses of snow? Have you seen the storehouses of hail?
38.23: Are they stored for you against the time of your enemies, For the day of wars and battles?
38.24: From where does the frost proceed? From where does the south wind scatter over the earth?
38.25: “Who prepared a course for the violent rain Or a path for the thunders?
38.26: Who causes it to rain on a land where there is no man, Or an uninhabited wilderness, where there is not a man in it,
38.27: To satisfy the untrodden and uninhabited land And cause it to spring forth a crop of tender grass?
38.28: Who is the rain's father, And who has begotten the drops of dew?
38.29: From whose womb comes the ice, And who has given birth to the frost in heaven,
38.30: Which descends like flowing water? Who made firm the face of the abyss?
38.31: “Do you understand the band of the Pleiades, And have you opened the fence of Orion?
38.32: Will you open up Mazzaroth in its season, And the evening star with his rays? Will you guide them?
38.33: Do you know the movem ents of heaven Or the events which take place together under heaven?
38.34: “Will you call a cloud with your voice, And will it obey you with a violent shower of much rain?
38.35: Can you send out lightnings, and they shall go? They shall say to you, ‘What do you want?’
38.36: Who has given to women wisdom in weaving Or knowledge of embroidery?
38.37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom, And who bowed heaven down to earth?
38.38: For it is spread like a cloud of dust, And I have joined it together as one hewn stone to another.
38.39: “Will you hunt prey for the lions Or satisfy the lives of the serpents?
38.40: They fear in their dens, And live in the forests, and lie in wait.
38.41: Who provides food for the raven? For its young ones wander And cry to the Lord in search of food.

39.1: “Do you know the time when the wild rock goats bear young, And do you mark when the deer gives birth?
39.2: Do you number the full months of child bearing, And have you relieved their pangs?
39.3: Have you reared their young without fear, And have you sent away their pangs?
39.4: Their young ones will break forth; They will be multiplied with offspring; They depart and do not return.
39.5: Who set the wild donkey free? Who loosed his bonds?
39.6: I made the wilderness his dwelling And the salt lands his house.
39.7: He scorns the great multitude of the city; He does not heed the blame of the tax collector.
39.8: He will survey the mountains as his pasture, And he seeks out every green thing.
39.9: Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will he bed by your manger?
39.10: Can you bind his yoke with ropes, Or will he plow furrows for you in the field?
39.11: Do you trust him because his strength is great? Or will you commit your works to him?
39.12: Will you trust him to bring home your seed And gather it to your threshing floor?
39.13: The wings of the falcon wave proudly, But are her wings and pinions like the kindly stork's?
39.14: For the falcon leaves her eggs on the ground And warms them in the dust.
39.15: She has forgotten that a foot will scatter them, Or that wild animals will trample them.
39.16: She hardens herself against her young ones As though they were not hers. She labors in vain without concern,
39.17: Because God deprived her of wisdom And did not endow her with understanding.
39.18: When she lifts herself on high, She scorns the horse and its rider.
39.19: Have you given the horse strength? Have you clothed his neck with a mane?
39.20: Have you put on him a suit of armor And made his breast glorious with courage?
39.21: He paws exultingly in the valley And goes forth with strength into the plain.
39.22: He mocks at battle when he sees it, Nor does he turn back from the sword.
39.23: The bow and the sword resound against him, And his rage would destroy the earth.
39.24: He will not believe until the trumpet sounds,
39.25: For at the blast of the trumpet he says, ‘Good! Well done!’ He smells the battle from afar with its leaping and shouting.
39.26: Does the hawk remain steadyby your understanding, And spread its rigid wings looking toward the south?
39.27: Does the eagle mount up at your command, And the vulture remain sitting over its nest
39.28: On the crag of a hidden rock?
39.29: From there it spies out the prey; Its eyes observe from afar.

40.1: Its young ones roll themselves in blood; And where the slain are, immediately they are found.” 40 Moreover the Lord God answered Job and said:
40.2: “Will anyone pervert judgment with the Mighty One? He who rebukes God will answer for it.” Job Responds
40.3: Then Job answered the Lord and said:
40.4: “Why am I still judged and admonished, Even if I rebuke the Lord, hear such things, and am nothing? But what answer will I give to these things? I will put my hand over my mouth.
40.5: I have spoken once. I will not do so a second time.” The Lord Calls Job to Account
40.6: The Lord yet answered Job out of the cloud and said:
40.7: “No rather, gird up your waist like a man, For I will question you, and you shall answer Me.
40.8: “Do you not reject My judgment? Do you think I have dealt with you in any other way Than might appear to you to be righteous?
40.9: Have you an arm like the Lord's? Or can you thunder with a voice like His?
40.10: Assume now majesty and power, And clothe yourself with glory and honor.
40.11: Send forth messengers with wrath And humble every insolent man.
40.12: Extinguish the arrogant man And consume at once the ungodly.
40.13: Hide them together in the earth And fill their faces with disgrace.
40.14: Then I will also admit That your own right hand can save you.
40.15: “But look now at the wild animals with you. They eat grass like oxen.
40.16: Behold now, his strength is in his loins, And his power is in the center of his stomach.
40.17: He sets up his tail like a cypress; His nerves are tightlyknit.
40.18: His ribs are like ribs of bronze, And his backbone like bars of iron.
40.19: This is the ruler of the Lord's creation, Made to be mocked at by His angels.
40.20: When he goes up to a rough mountain, He causes joy to the four-footed animals in Tartarus.
40.21: He lies under trees of every kind, Alongside the papyrus, and reed, and bulrush.
40.22: The great trees shade him with their branches; So do the branches of the willow.
40.23: If there should be a flood, he will not notice it; He is confident, though the Jordan beats against his mouth,
40.24: Though he takes it in his eyes, Or one pierces his nose with a snare.
40.25: Will you catch the serpent with a hook And put a halter about his nose?
40.26: Or will you fasten a ring in his nose Or pierce his lip with a hook?
40.27: Will he speak to you in prayer, Softly with the voice of a suppliant?
40.28: Will he make a covenant with you? Will you take him as a servant forever?
40.29: Will you play with him as with a bird, Or will you cage him as a sparrow for a child?
40.30: Do the nations feed upon him? Will they apportion him am ong the nations of the Phoenicians?
40.31: All the ships come together would not be able To bear the mere skin of his tail, Or carry his head with fishing vessels.
40.32: Once you lay your hand on him, Remembering the battle waged by his mouth, Let it not be done again.

41.1: “Hav e you not seen him? Have you not wondered at what has been said of him?
41.2: Do you not fear because I am prepared? Who then is able to stand against Me?
41.3: Who will stand against Me and endure, Since everything under heaven is Mine?
41.4: “I will not be silent because of him, Though because of his power, one shall pity his antagonist.
41.5: Who will remove his outer coat? Who may enter within the fold of his breastplate?
41.6: Who will open the doors of his face, With his terrible teeth all around?
41.7: His entrails are as brazen plates, And the texture of his skin as a symrite stone.
41.8: One part clings to another So no air comes between them.
41.9: A man will be joined to his brother. They stick together and cannot be parted.
41.10: His sneezings flash forth light, And his eyes are like the appearance of the morning star.
41.11: Out of his mouth go burning lights; Sparks of fire shoot out.
41.12: Smoke goes out of his nostrils As from a boiling pot with fire of coals.
41.13: His breath kindles coals, And a flame goes out of his mouth.
41.14: Strength dwells in his neck, And destruction runs before him.
41.15: The muscles of his body are joined together. They are firm on him and cannot be moved.
41.16: His heart is as hard as stone, And it stands like an unyielding anvil.
41.17: When he turns, he is a terror To the four-footed wild animals which leap upon the earth.
41.18: Though the sword reaches him, it cannot avail; Nor does spear or javelin.
41.19: He regards iron as straw, And bronze as rotten wood.
41.20: The arrow cannot wound him; The sling-stone becomes like grass to him.
41.21: Hammers are regarded as straw, And he laughs at the threat of javelins.
41.22: His bed is like sharp skewers, And all the gold of the sea under him Is like a great amount of clay.
41.23: He makes the deep boil like a brazen pot, And he regards the sea like a pot of ointment.
41.24: The lowest part of the deep is as a captive. He reckons the deep as his walking range.
41.25: On earth there is nothing like him, Who was made to be mocked at by My angels.
41.26: He beholds every high thing; He is king over all that are in the waters.” Job's Confession and Repentance

42.1: Then Job answered the Lord and said:
42.2: “I know You can do all things, And nothing is impossible for You.
42.3: For who is he who hides counsel from You? Who keeps back his words And thinks to hide them from You? Who will tell me what I knew not, Things too great and wonderful, which I did not know?
42.4: But hear me, O Lord, that I also may speak. I will ask You, and please teach Me.
42.5: “I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear, But now my eye sees You.
42.6: Therefore I depreciate myself, and I waste away. I regard myself as dust and ashes.” The Lord Rebukes and Redeems Job's Friends
42.7: So it was, after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, that the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You have sinned, you and your two friends, for you have not spoken before Me what is true, as My servant Job has.
42.8: Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you. For I will only accept him, but for his sake, I would have destroyed you; because you have not spoken what is true regarding my servant Job.”
42.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Lord commanded them; and He redeemed their sin for Job's sake. Job's Wealth Is Restored
42.10: Then the Lord restored Job's losses when he prayed for his friends, and He forgave their sin. But the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
42.11: Then all his brothers and all his sisters heard about everything that happened to him, and they came to him. So did all who knew him from the first. They ate food and drank with him and comforted him; and they wondered at all the Lord brought upon him. Each one gave him a lamb and four drachms’ weight of uncoined gold.
42.12: Now the Lord blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand donkeys.
42.13: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
42.14: And he named the first, Day, the second, Cassia, and the third, Amalthia's Horn.
42.15: In all the land, there were found no women so beautiful as the daughters of Job, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
42.16: After this affliction, Job lived one hundred and seventy years, and all the years he lived were two hundred forty-eight; and Job saw his children and gr and children for four generations.
42.17: So Job died, old and full of days.
42.18: It is written that he will rise with those whom the Lord resurrects.
42.19: This man is described in the Syriac book as living in the land of Ausitis, on the borders of Edom and Arabia. Previously his name was Jobab.
42.20: He took an Arabian wife and begot a son named Ennon. But he himself was the son of his father Zare, one of the sons of Esau, and of his mother, Bosorra. Thus, he was the fifth son from Abraham.
42.21: Now these were the kings who reigned in Edom, over which country he also ruled. First, there was Balak the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dennaba. But after Balak, there was Jobab, who is called Job. After him, there was Asom, who was ruler out of the country of Teman. After him, there was Adad the son of Barad, who destroyed Midian in the plain of Moab; and the name of his city was Gethaim.
42.22: Now his friends who came to him were: Eliphaz, of the children of Esau, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minians.
